hero.headline: Judge blocks Trump's changes to Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge has ordered the removal of Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, ruling that the prestigious Washington DC venue cannot be renamed without congressional action.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper directed the Trump administration to take down all physical signage bearing Trump's name and eliminate references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" from official materials within 14 days. In his 94-page opinion, Cooper stated that the Kennedy Center's founding law makes clear the institution must be named for President Kennedy and cannot bear any other formal name based on unilateral board decisions.

"Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it," Cooper wrote. The judge concluded that the board of trustees overstepped its legal authority by attempting to rename the center after Trump.

Trump responded swiftly on his Truth Social platform, announcing he had instructed the Department of Commerce to arrange a complete transfer of the Kennedy Center to Congress. He suggested that unless he remained free to renovate and restore the institution, he had no interest in continuing with it.

The ruling also temporarily blocked a proposed two-month summer closure for renovations that Trump had announced. Judge Cooper found the board's decision to halt operations was inadequately researched and neglected to consider the institution's statutory obligations. He characterized the closure decision as "ill-informed and seemingly preordained."

The lawsuit was brought by Joyce Beatty, an Ohio Democratic representative and member of the Kennedy Center's board. She called the ruling a vindication of efforts to prevent what she described as Trump's attempt to use the institution for personal vanity. "The Kennedy Center is an institution that belongs to the American people, not to Donald Trump," Beatty said.

The dispute began after Trump took office and appointed himself chair of the Kennedy Center's board of trustees in February, calling it a "take-over." He removed existing board members and replaced them with his appointees. In December, the reconstituted board voted to add Trump's name to the institution.

The attempt to rename the center sparked significant backlash. Artists and performing groups canceled bookings in protest, including the Tony award-winning musical Hamilton. The National Symphony Orchestra's executive director left her position, and Richard Grenell, a Trump appointee who championed the overhaul, announced his resignation as president in March.

The Kennedy Center, which receives federal funding, has long enjoyed bipartisan support as one of the nation's leading arts venues. Under Trump's leadership, it has become an extension of the White House's cultural agenda, hosting events from the World Cup draw to House Republican addresses and the premiere of a documentary about First Lady Melania Trump.

cards.headline: Iran ceasefire talks show no progress as negotiations continue
cards.teaser: Efforts to extend a ceasefire with Iran have not advanced, according to recent discussions of the diplomatic situation.
cards.body:
A report of an extended ceasefire with Iran, pending President Trump's approval, has caused global oil prices to fall. However, Trump has not yet made a decision on whether to extend the ceasefire agreement. Core issues in the negotiations remain unresolved.

Meanwhile, President Trump has offered to perform at the Freedom 250 festival, which marks America's 250th birthday. The offer comes as organizers seek to fill the event's lineup after several major musical acts withdrew from the celebration.

cards.headline: Israeli military captures Beaufort Castle in Lebanon offensive
cards.teaser: Israel seized the strategic Beaufort Castle as its ground offensive in Lebanon expands southward.
cards.body:
The Israeli military has captured Beaufort Castle, a strategically important position in southern Lebanon. Following the seizure, the military ordered all residents south of the Zahrani river to evacuate the area.

The castle, built during the Crusader period, sits in a key location as Israel's ground offensive deepens into Lebanon's southern territory. The expansion of Israel's military operations continues as forces advance further into the country.

cards.headline: Newark mayor orders curfew around immigration detention center after days of clashes
cards.body:
Newark Mayor Ras Baraka ordered a curfew around Delaney Hall, an immigration detention center, after days of clashes between protesters and law enforcement officers. The mayor said the measure was necessary to ensure the safety and well-being of all residents.

The mandatory curfew covers a half-mile area surrounding the facility and took effect immediately. The order was issued on Sunday.

Protesters and police have been clashing at the site for several days. The detention center has become a flashpoint as the Trump administration increases deportation efforts.

Baraka, a Democrat, did not specify how long the curfew would remain in place or provide details about injuries or arrests during the confrontations. The curfew restricts movement in the designated area during specified hours, though the exact timeframe was not detailed in available information.

The clashes at Delaney Hall reflect broader tensions over immigration enforcement policies. Newark, New Jersey's largest city, has seen increased activity around immigration detention as federal authorities expand operations.

The mayor's decision to impose a geographic curfew rather than a citywide measure suggests officials are trying to contain the situation while minimizing disruption to the wider community. Law enforcement presence in the area has been significant as authorities work to manage the ongoing demonstrations.

The situation in Newark mirrors confrontations at other immigration facilities across the country as the administration pursues more aggressive deportation policies. Local officials in several cities have faced difficult decisions about how to balance public safety concerns with residents' rights to protest.

Baraka has not announced additional measures beyond the curfew. The restriction applies to both protesters and other residents within the half-mile radius of the detention center.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The Department of Justice has launched a criminal investigation originating from U.S. Attorneys offices, raising questions about the probe's origins.
cards.body:
Former federal prosecutor Ankush Khardori discussed the Justice Department's criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, calling the probe's structure uncommon. The investigation originated from U.S. Attorneys offices around the country rather than through typical channels.

Khardori, who previously worked as a federal prosecutor, explained why such investigations and prosecutions initiated at the local U.S. Attorney level are considered outside normal procedures. The case has drawn attention from legal observers tracking Justice Department activities.

cards.headline: Trump administration proposes nondisclosure agreements for federal workers
cards.teaser: The White House plan to require NDAs for government employees has drawn criticism from those who say it would silence the workforce.
cards.body:
The Office of Personnel Management proposed requiring both new and existing federal employees to sign nondisclosure agreements. The plan has generated accusations that the administration is attempting to prevent federal workers from speaking to the press.

OPM announced the proposal on Tuesday as part of efforts to manage information flow from government agencies. Critics argue the NDAs would restrict employees' ability to communicate about their work and government operations.

cards.headline: Schools face movement against classroom screens and devices
cards.teaser: A book has fueled pushback against technology in education as classrooms shift to analog learning.
cards.body:
A growing movement is challenging the widespread use of screens and technology in schools. A book has become central to efforts pushing back against school-assigned devices, from Chromebooks to iPads.

Classrooms are beginning to lean into analog learning methods as the artificial intelligence era advances. The Teachers Union has urged schools to reduce AI chatbot access and limit screen time for students.

hero.headline: Nearly 800 arrested in France after riots following Champions League final
hero.body:
French police arrested nearly 800 people after violent clashes erupted following the Champions League final. The riots left 219 people injured, including 57 police officers.

The arrests came after widespread disorder in France. Police confronted crowds in multiple locations as celebrations turned violent.

The Champions League final sparked the unrest. Paris Saint-Germain fans took to the streets after their team's victory, but celebrations quickly escalated into clashes with law enforcement.

Fifty-seven police officers were among those injured during the confrontations. The total injury count of 219 people reflects the scale of the violence that unfolded.

French authorities made 780 arrests in connection with the riots. Police worked to contain the disorder as it spread across affected areas.

The violence marked one of the largest public order incidents in recent French history. Law enforcement deployed significant resources to manage the unrest and restore order.

Officials have not released details about charges facing those arrested. The investigation into the riots continues as authorities work to identify all those responsible for the violence.

The incident raises questions about security planning for major sporting events. French police have faced criticism in the past for their handling of large crowds at high-profile matches.

The injury toll among both civilians and police reflects the intensity of the clashes. Medical services responded to numerous calls throughout the night as the violence unfolded.

Authorities are now assessing the damage caused during the riots. The cleanup effort began as police maintained a presence in affected areas to prevent further outbreaks of violence.

The PSG victory came after a closely contested match. The final demonstrated the passion that major European football competitions generate among supporters, though the celebrations descended into disorder in the streets of Paris.

Security experts have noted that managing crowds at major sporting events requires careful planning and coordination between law enforcement agencies. The scale of arrests following this incident suggests authorities took an aggressive approach to restoring order.

The aftermath of the riots will likely prompt discussions about how to better manage celebrations following major sporting victories. Event organizers and police forces across Europe may review their protocols based on what occurred in Paris.

Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances that led to the escalation of violence. They are working to understand how the initial celebrations transformed into widespread disorder requiring hundreds of arrests.

The incident has drawn attention to the challenges posed by large gatherings of passionate sports fans. While most supporters celebrate peacefully, even a fraction engaging in violence can create significant public safety challenges for law enforcement agencies.

French police are expected to release additional details about the arrests and resulting charges in the coming weeks as the investigation progresses.

The Israeli military has captured Beaufort Castle, a strategically important position in southern Lebanon. Following the seizure, the military ordered all residents south of the Zahrani river to evacuate the area.

cards.headline: Retired Nigerian general and wife kidnapped in country's northwest
cards.teaser: Maj Gen Rabe Abubakar and his wife were abducted in northwestern Nigeria.
cards.body:
Maj Gen Rabe Abubakar, a retired Nigerian general, was abducted along with his wife in the northwest region of the country. The kidnapping underscores the ongoing security challenges that have affected parts of Nigeria.

Northwestern areas have faced persistent threats from armed groups and criminal activity in recent years, making this incident part of a broader pattern of instability in the region.

cards.headline: Five rescued from flooded Laos cave as search continues for two missing men
cards.teaser: Survivors are helping authorities plan the search for two men still trapped in a narrow, flooded cave in Laos.
cards.body:
Five men have been rescued from a narrow, flooded cave in Laos. Two of the seven villagers who entered the tunnels on 20 May while searching for gold remain missing.

The freed survivors are now helping to develop a strategy to locate the two men still trapped inside. Rescue operations have been hampered by the cave's tight passages and water flooding.

cards.headline: South African football team delayed for World Cup over visa problems
cards.teaser: South Africa's sports minister says visa issues have made the country look foolish as the national team's departure to Mexico is delayed.
cards.body:
South Africa's national football team faced delays in departing for the World Cup in Mexico due to visa complications. The country's sports minister criticized the situation, saying it made South Africa appear incompetent.

The football association confirmed it was working to resolve the issues preventing the team's travel and disrupting their tournament preparations.

cards.headline: Colombia holds presidential election testing leftist legacy against far-right challenger
cards.teaser: Colombian voters are choosing between candidates representing the legacy of the country's first leftist leader, a far-right outsider, and a traditional conservative.
cards.body:
Colombians are voting in the first round of a presidential election that will determine the country's direction after a decade of peace efforts. The vote serves as a referendum on outgoing leftist President Gustavo Petro's policies, ten years after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc).

The election comes amid tension between Petro and US President Donald Trump. Candidates hold sharply different visions for Colombia's future, with pro-Trump contenders competing alongside an ally of the outgoing leftist leader in a race that will shape the nation's approach to peace and stability.

cards.headline: Coastal residents in Colombia and Ecuador reconsider ocean livelihoods after US boat strikes
cards.teaser: More than 200 deaths from US boat strikes have prompted coastal communities to rethink fishing and maritime work.
cards.body:
Residents of coastal communities in Colombia and Ecuador are reconsidering ocean-based work following an airstrike campaign. The campaign has resulted in over 200 deaths from US boat strikes, prompting fishing communities and others dependent on maritime employment to reassess their futures in these industries.

Beyond the death toll, local residents report the campaign has caused broader damage to their communities and way of life.

cards.teaser: The Israeli military ordered evacuations south of the Zahrani river after seizing the strategic castle.
cards.body:
The Israeli military has captured Beaufort Castle, a strategic location in Lebanon, as it continues its ground offensive in the country. The seizure of the castle represents a significant expansion of Israeli military operations across the border.

Following the capture, Israeli forces issued an evacuation order for all civilians south of the Zahrani river, indicating the scope of the military campaign in the region.

cards.headline: Nearly 800 arrested in Champions League riots in France
cards.teaser: Clashes with police left 219 people injured, including 57 officers.
cards.body:
Nearly 800 people were arrested following clashes with police after a Champions League match in France. The violence left 219 people injured, including 57 police officers.

The scale of the disorder represents one of the most significant instances of football-related violence in recent years.

cards.teaser: Competitive midterm contests put Iowa at the center of the battle for Congress.
cards.body: Iowa holds its primary election Tuesday, with both Democrats and Republicans viewing the state as crucial to determining which party will control Congress. While Iowa traditionally receives attention during presidential elections, this year's midterm contests have emerged as surprisingly competitive, elevating the state's importance for both parties in their efforts to gain congressional control.

cards.teaser: The election follows months of public conflict between President Gustavo Petro and Donald Trump.

Colombia held a presidential election following months of public disagreement between left-wing President Gustavo Petro and US President Donald Trump. The vote has the potential to reshape Colombian-American relations going forward.

The outcome of the election will likely influence the direction of ties between the two countries in the coming years.

cards.headline: Reality TV stars increasingly run for political office
cards.teaser: Some reality show celebrities use their fame as a path to running for political positions.
cards.body:
Reality television stars are increasingly using their fame as a springboard into politics. The genre, known for its dramatic and sometimes frivolous entertainment value, has become an unexpected pathway for candidates seeking elected office.

Stars who participate in reality shows gain experience managing their public image and navigating high-pressure situations. Many leverage the visibility and platform they've built through television to launch political campaigns, treating their reality TV experience as preparation for the demands of public service.

hero.headline: Chinese Lung Cancer Drug Cuts Death Risk by 34% in Late-Stage Trial
hero.body:
A combination drug developed by Chinese pharmaceutical company Akeso in partnership with Summit Therapeutics reduced the risk of death by 34% in a late-stage clinical trial, according to results presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology conference.

The drug, ivonescimab, was tested in patients with squamous cell lung cancer, a subtype of non-small cell lung cancer. Researchers compared ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy against a standard PD-1 inhibitor also given with chemotherapy. Patients receiving ivonescimab experienced longer survival times than those on the comparison treatment.

Ivonescimab works through a dual mechanism, combining two distinct treatment approaches. The drug includes a PD-1 inhibitor, which activates the immune system to fight cancer cells, and a VEGF inhibitor, which blocks the blood vessel growth that tumors require to survive. This two-pronged strategy represents an emerging trend in cancer medicine where drugs target multiple biological pathways simultaneously.

The trial results have generated considerable discussion within the medical community. The drug has been described as hotly debated, though specific details about the controversy remain unclear from the trial data itself.

Squamous cell carcinoma represents a significant portion of lung cancer diagnoses, particularly among smokers. Lung cancer continues to rank among the most common and deadliest cancers worldwide. Current treatment approaches typically involve combinations of chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and targeted medications.

The results unveiled at ASCO, an annual conference where major pharmaceutical companies present clinical trial findings, could have implications extending beyond Akeso and Summit. Other companies developing similar dual-pathway cancer treatments will likely monitor how ivonescimab performs through regulatory review processes and potential approval. The trial outcomes may influence development strategies across the oncology industry.

The dual action of blocking both PD-1 and VEGF pathways represents a strategic approach to combating cancer from multiple angles. By simultaneously enhancing immune activation and restricting tumor blood supply, the medication aims to attack the disease more effectively than single-pathway treatments.

As ivonescimab moves forward in the regulatory process, the trial's results could shape how other pharmaceutical companies approach cancer drug development. The 34% reduction in death risk demonstrates the potential value of combination approaches targeting multiple mechanisms within tumors. Companies developing competing treatments will be watching closely to understand how this strategy performs in real-world use and whether similar combinations might offer comparable benefits for patients with other cancer types.

The trial represents an important step toward expanding treatment options for squamous cell lung cancer patients, a population with limited effective therapies.

cards.headline: China's Factory Activity Stalls in May as Demand Weakens
cards.teaser: Manufacturing activity in China showed no growth in May as demand for goods declined.
cards.body:
Factory activity in China stalled during May, with data indicating a halt in manufacturing growth. The slowdown reflected weakening demand for goods produced in Chinese factories.

China's manufacturing sector serves as a key indicator of the country's economic health and global trade flows. The stalled activity suggests reduced orders and production levels compared to previous months, pointing to broader economic headwinds affecting the world's second-largest economy.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Tries to Breach Cockpit
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted after a passenger attempted multiple times to enter the cockpit.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight heading to Minneapolis was forced to divert to Madison, Wisconsin after a 75-year-old man made multiple attempts to breach the cockpit. The incident occurred on United flight 2005 departing from Chicago, prompting a hijacking alert.

The man was removed from the aircraft after the emergency landing in Madison. One passenger described the incident as not violent. The flight was carrying passengers who witnessed the disruption before the plane was diverted for safety reasons.

cards.headline: Beer Industry Looks to World Cup to Reverse Sales Decline
cards.teaser: The maker of Budweiser is betting heavily on the soccer tournament to boost beer sales, though bars and stores remain uncertain.
cards.body:
The U.S. beer industry is hoping the World Cup will help reverse a sales slump, with major brewers making significant investments in the tournament. The maker of Budweiser and Michelob Ultra is committing substantial resources to World Cup marketing and promotions.

Bars and retail stores expressed uncertainty about whether the soccer tournament will actually increase beer sales. Despite the mixed expectations from sellers, the brewer is proceeding with an all-in strategy tied to the global sporting event.

cards.headline: Joby Conducts Electric Air Taxi Test Flight in Manhattan
cards.teaser: An aviation startup demonstrated an all-electric aircraft over New York City, though public flights remain years away.
cards.body:
Joby Aviation demonstrated its electric air taxi over Manhattan in a test flight, showcasing how the aircraft could operate in an urban environment. The demonstration represents progress toward the company's goal of replacing traditional helicopters with battery-powered aircraft.

The vehicle is not yet available for passenger use. Before the service can launch commercially, the aircraft must complete extensive testing and obtain regulatory approval. Aviation startups and the Trump administration are backing the development of electric aircraft as helicopter alternatives, though safety certification requirements mean public flights remain some time away.

cards.headline: Airbnb Expands Beyond Home Rentals to Car Rentals, Groceries, and Hotels
cards.teaser: The home-sharing platform added car rentals, grocery delivery, and hotel bookings as CEO Brian Chesky continues redesigning the app.
cards.body:
Airbnb recently expanded its services to include car rentals, groceries, and hotels, moving beyond its original focus on home sharing. The additions represent a significant shift in strategy for the platform, with hotels being the most surprising category given Airbnb's history as a hotel alternative.

Co-founder and CEO Brian Chesky is driving the redesign of the app and its service offerings. Chesky continues to rethink what Airbnb can be as a platform, expanding into adjacent travel and convenience services that complement accommodation bookings.

cards.headline: Former Marks & Spencer Chief to Advise Government on Youth Unemployment
cards.teaser: Marc Bolland will help the government address youth joblessness after a review warned of a lost generation.
cards.body:
Marc Bolland, the former chief executive of Marks & Spencer, has been appointed to advise the government on tackling youth unemployment. The move follows a review that identified a potential "lost generation" of young people unable to find work.

Bolland will work on developing strategies to help young people enter employment, drawing on his experience in the retail sector to support government efforts to address rising joblessness among younger workers.

hero.headline: Microsoft threatens security researchers with criminal investigation over exploit disclosure
hero.body:
Microsoft has come under fire for threatening security researchers with criminal investigation after they disclosed software vulnerabilities in the company's products, according to multiple reports. The dispute has reignited a broader debate about who bears responsibility for securing software.

The controversy centers on how Microsoft has responded to independent security researchers who discovered and reported flaws. Kevin Beaumont, a prominent security researcher, has been vocal about his experience, describing feeling humiliated by the company's approach. He has stated that Microsoft threatened to ruin his life over the disclosure of exploits. The threats reportedly involved potential criminal action against those who found the vulnerabilities.

Major technology news outlets have covered the dispute extensively. TechCrunch reported that Microsoft came under fire for threatening a security researcher with criminal investigation. The Verge described Microsoft threatening legal action for disclosing exploits. The Register reported that Microsoft called law enforcement on a researcher, characterizing them as disgruntled.

Beaumont has been particularly critical of Microsoft's overall approach, arguing on his blog that the company's stance on zero day exploits represents a failure of Microsoft's own making. Zero day exploits are security vulnerabilities unknown to the software maker with no available patch or fix.

The incident raises fundamental questions about how major technology companies should handle security research and vulnerability disclosure. Security researchers generally argue that their work improves software safety by identifying flaws before malicious actors can exploit them. Companies, however, sometimes view unauthorized security testing as a potential violation of their terms of service or as a security threat.

Microsoft maintains bug bounty programs that compensate researchers for discovering certain types of vulnerabilities. However, significant disagreement persists within the security research community about what types of disclosures qualify for payment versus legal threats or other company responses.

The dispute highlights ongoing tension between technology companies and security researchers over responsible disclosure practices. Researchers typically follow protocols by reporting flaws to companies before making them public, giving software makers time to develop patches. The disagreement centers on how companies should treat researchers who deviate from these processes or who disclose information without company permission.

Microsoft has not publicly commented on the specific threats described by Beaumont and other researchers involved in the dispute. The company's handling of the situation has drawn attention from those who follow cybersecurity issues and technology policy, with many viewing it as emblematic of broader challenges in how the industry manages vulnerability research and disclosure.

cards.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, triggering sonic boom heard across New England
cards.teaser: A meteor exploded over Massachusetts, creating loud booms heard by hundreds of people across New England and sightings reported from Delaware to Montreal.
cards.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating sonic booms that reverberated across the region. The blast was equivalent to 300 tons of TNT, according to NASA.

The meteor was traveling at 75,000 miles per hour when it broke apart at an altitude of 40 miles. The explosion was heard and felt by hundreds of residents across multiple states in the northeastern United States.

cards.headline: James Bond game First Light becomes major sales success
cards.teaser: The new James Bond video game First Light has become a significant sales hit, with some calling it the Bond game fans have been waiting for.
cards.body:
The video game 007 First Light has become a major commercial success since its launch across PC, Xbox, and PlayStation 5. Developer IO Interactive, known for the Hitman assassination series, created the game as a prequel exploring Bond's early career before he earned his 00 status.

IO Interactive brought its signature expertise in stealth gameplay and globe-trotting narratives to the Bond franchise. The developer's experience crafting sophisticated, architecturally detailed environments and morally complex protagonists positioned it well to reimagine the iconic character for a new generation of players.

cards.headline: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 images leak, showing wider design
cards.teaser: Leaked images compare Samsung's upcoming Galaxy Z Fold 8 to an Ultra model, showing a wider frame design.
cards.body:
A leaked photograph shows Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 alongside what appears to be an Ultra variant, revealing design differences between the two models. The wider Galaxy Z Fold 8 frame was visible in the comparison image published by technology news sites.

Reports indicate Samsung will use Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra branding for the upcoming foldable phone lineup. The display crease on the Z Fold 8 series is expected to match the quality of Oppo's Find N6, according to reports. Android Central covered charging speed specifications for the new device.

cards.headline: Blue moon visible across United States under clear skies
cards.teaser: The second full moon of May, known as a blue moon, rose over the United States with clear viewing conditions in many areas.
cards.body:
A blue moon, the second full moon occurring in May, became visible across the United States. Clear skies in many regions provided good viewing conditions for the astronomical event.

Metro Detroit experienced clear weather that allowed residents to view the blue moon. CNN and PBS provided guidance on how and when to watch the rare blue micromoon. Space covered where and when to see the second full moon of May as it rose over different parts of the country.

cards.headline: Paint.net software now available at Paint.net web address after 22 years
cards.teaser: The graphics editing software Paint.net can now be downloaded from the URL Paint.net, 22 years after the program was first released.
cards.body:
Paint.net, a graphics editing program, became available for download at the web address Paint.net after more than two decades of the software's existence. XDA reported that users can now access the software directly from the domain name that matches the program's name.

The change occurred 22 years after Paint.net was originally released. The software had previously been available through other web addresses before obtaining the Paint.net domain.

cards.headline: Rising temperatures affect animal behavior and learning ability
cards.teaser: Heat affects animal cognition, causing some creatures to become more aggressive while others struggle to learn new tasks.
cards.body:
Scientists have documented how rising temperatures affect animal brains and behavior. Some creatures become more aggressive and pick fights in hot conditions, while others experience difficulty learning.

The effects of heat on animal cognition vary by species. Researchers use the term stupid hot to describe conditions that muddle animal brain function and alter normal behavior patterns.

hero.headline: San Antonio Spurs beat Oklahoma City Thunder to reach NBA Finals
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night, earning their place in the NBA Finals against the New York Knicks. Game 1 is scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory with 22 points and seven rebounds, earning him the series MVP award. The 22-year-old French center became emotional after the game, reflecting on the significance of the achievement.

"Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," Wembanyama said when asked about his emotional reaction. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

However, the victory was not solely attributable to Wembanyama's performance. Julian Champagnie contributed 20 points and made six three-pointers, while Dylan Harper made impactful plays off the bench. Luke Kornet, Wembanyama's backup, delivered a crucial block in the fourth quarter as Oklahoma City mounted a comeback attempt.

"They don't know how much I love them, and everyone stepped up tonight," Wembanyama said of his teammates.

The Thunder, playing without Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury, fought throughout the contest. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, was exceptional for Oklahoma City, scoring 35 points and recording nine assists. However, no other Thunder player scored more than 20 points, ultimately proving insufficient against the Spurs' balanced attack.

As the game concluded, Oklahoma City was forced to take desperate three-point attempts from well beyond the arc, while San Antonio sealed the victory with a breakaway dunk.

Thunder coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the difficult loss while maintaining confidence in his team's future. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he said. "And it's the NBA, there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

The Spurs' advance to the Finals represents a remarkable turnaround for the franchise, which has rebuilt around its young core. This matchup carries historical significance, as the last time the Knicks appeared in the NBA Finals was in 1999, when they faced the Spurs. San Antonio won that series 4-1.

Champagnie expressed confidence in his team's prospects moving forward. "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen," he said.

The Spurs will look to carry their momentum into the Finals as they face New York.

cards.headline: Nearly 800 arrested after Champions League riots in France
cards.teaser: Police arrested 780 people and reported 219 injuries, including 57 officers, after violence following Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory.
cards.body:
Nearly 800 people were arrested following clashes with police after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory. The unrest left 219 people injured, including 57 police officers.

The riots erupted across Paris as fans took to the streets to celebrate PSG's win. Multiple fires were set throughout the city during the disorder.

cards.headline: Marta Kostyuk defeats four-time champion Iga Swiatek at French Open
cards.teaser: Iga Swiatek lost to Marta Kostyuk in the fourth round of the French Open, ending the four-time champion's tournament run.
cards.body:
Marta Kostyuk delivered a stunning upset over No. 3 seed Iga Swiatek in the fourth round at Roland Garros, winning 7-5, 6-1. The Ukrainian 15th seed's dominant performance eliminated the last remaining former champion from the women's draw and marked one of the worst performances of Swiatek's career at the tournament.

The loss came on Swiatek's 25th birthday, ending a run that had seen the Polish champion win four French Open titles in five years. Kostyuk's victory caps a superb recent run of form at the tournament.

cards.headline: Amanda Serrano equals knockout record with second-round stoppage
cards.teaser: Amanda Serrano stopped Cheyenne Hanson in the second round to tie the record for most knockouts in women's boxing history while retaining her featherweight titles.
cards.body:
Amanda Serrano made history in Texas, equaling the record for most knockouts in women's boxing with a second-round stoppage of Cheyenne Hanson. The dominant performance allowed Serrano to successfully defend her WBA and WBO featherweight titles.

Serrano controlled the fight from the start, bringing the bout to a quick conclusion and reaching the historic knockout milestone.

cards.headline: Aryna Sabalenka to play Naomi Osaka in first French Open women's night match since 2023
cards.teaser: Aryna Sabalenka's fourth-round match against Naomi Osaka will be the first women's match in the French Open night session since 2023.
cards.body:
Aryna Sabalenka will face Naomi Osaka in a fourth-round French Open match on Monday that will be played during the tournament's night session. This marks the first women's match scheduled in the night slot at Roland Garros since 2023.

The French Open had not scheduled women's matches in the evening time slot in the intervening years. The decision to feature Sabalenka and Osaka's match in prime time represents a return to scheduling women's tennis in the night session.

cards.headline: Transgender athlete AB Hernandez wins two state titles at California track meet
cards.teaser: Jurupa Valley senior AB Hernandez won two medals at the California state track and field championships amid ongoing debate.
cards.body:
AB Hernandez, a transgender senior from Jurupa Valley, captured two state titles at the California track and field championships, capping off her high school athletic career with the victories.

The championships drew protests related to transgender athlete participation in the sport. Hernandez's mother spoke publicly during the meet, which took place in Fresno.

cards.headline: Great Britain wins first rowing golds of season in Seville
cards.teaser: British rowers claimed their first gold medals of the 2026 season at the World Rowing Cup in Seville.
cards.body:
Great Britain won its first gold medals of the season at the 2026 World Rowing Cup I in Seville. The victories mark the beginning of the British rowing team's international competition season.

The World Rowing Cup serves as a key preparation event for rowers ahead of major championships. British crews demonstrated strong early-season form in Spain.

hero.headline: Matt Brown, Star of Alaskan Bush People, Dies at 43
hero.body:
Matt Brown, who starred in the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People, has died at 43. His body was pulled from a river, according to multiple reports.

Brown appeared on Alaskan Bush People, which followed the lives of the Brown family living in remote Alaska. The show documented their efforts to build and maintain homesteads in wilderness areas.

According to reports, Brown's brother Noah helped pull his body from the river. Another brother, Bear Brown, had previously posted that Matt had been seen near a river where police said a man went missing.

Matt Brown was the oldest of the seven Brown siblings featured on the show. The series premiered in 2014 and followed the family as they lived off the grid in various locations in Alaska and later Washington state.

The Discovery Channel series became one of the network's most watched programs during its run. The show featured the family's patriarch Billy Brown, who died in 2021, and matriarch Ami Brown, along with their children.

Brown had previously left the series for periods of time. He appeared in earlier seasons of the show before stepping away from regular appearances in later years.

The circumstances surrounding his death are still being investigated by authorities. The family has not yet released an official statement about the loss.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Contestant After Video Shows Use of Racial Slur
cards.teaser: Peacock removed a cast member from Love Island USA Season 8 after videos surfaced showing the contestant using a racial slur.
cards.body:
Love Island USA dismissed cast member Vasana Montgomery from the upcoming eighth season after videos surfaced on social media showing her using a racial slur. The removal occurred shortly before the season's June 2 premiere on Peacock.

This is the second consecutive year the dating competition series has removed a contestant for the same reason. The show features single contestants living together in a villa while competing for a cash prize.

cards.headline: Italy Bans Kanye West and Travis Scott Concerts Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Italian authorities canceled scheduled concerts by Kanye West and Travis Scott in Reggio Emilia, citing security issues.
cards.body:
Kanye West's concert scheduled for July 18 at the RCF Arena in Reggio Emilia has been cancelled by the city's prefect, Salvatore Angieri, over public order and safety concerns. Travis Scott was also set to perform at the same venue as part of the Pulse of Gaia festival.

The cancellation came after concerns raised by the local Jewish community regarding West's previous antisemitic remarks. Italian authorities determined that proceeding with the performances would pose risks to public safety in the northern city.

cards.headline: Brazil Launches Free Government Streaming Service With 555 Productions
cards.teaser: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced Tela Brasil, a free public streaming platform featuring Brazilian content.
cards.body:
Tela Brasil, a free public streaming service, was announced by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva at the Rio2C conference. The platform launched with a catalog of 555 Brazilian productions available at no cost.

Anyone with an account on Gov.br, the official digital platform of the Brazilian federal government, can access the service. The announcement took place in Rio de Janeiro.

cards.headline: Trump Says He Will Perform at Freedom 250 Concert After Artist Cancellations
cards.teaser: Donald Trump offered to headline the Freedom 250 concert himself after multiple artists withdrew from the event.
cards.body:
Donald Trump offered to perform at the Freedom 250 concert series, stating that only great patriots would be invited. The announcement followed a wave of artist withdrawals from the event, organized by the Trump administration to mark the nation's 250th anniversary.

At least seven of nine featured musical acts dropped out within 48 hours of the lineup announcement. Artists including Young MC, Bret Michaels and Martina McBride cited concerns about the event's political nature, with Michaels specifically mentioning threats and a deteriorating atmosphere surrounding the concert series.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Flips Piano During Denver Concert
cards.teaser: Country singer Morgan Wallen overturned a piano onstage during a performance in Denver.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen flipped over a piano during a concert in Denver. The incident occurred while he was performing his song Sand in My Boots.

Reports indicate the country star appeared upset with the instrument during the performance. The onstage moment drew comparisons to Billy Joel's past stage antics.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Performs at Philadelphia Roots Picnic With Jazmine Sullivan and Meek Mill
cards.teaser: Jay-Z headlined the Roots Picnic in Philadelphia, joined by Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal, and Meek Mill.
cards.body:
Jay-Z headlined the Roots Picnic in Philadelphia, taking the stage with several guest artists. Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal, and Meek Mill joined him for the performance.

Ahead of the show, Jay-Z changed his streaming name from Jay-Z back to its original spelling, JA-Z, signaling a shift he had been preparing for in recent months.

hero.headline: Newark mayor orders curfew around immigration detention center after days of clashes
hero.body:
Newark Mayor Ras Baraka ordered a curfew around Delaney Hall, an immigration detention center, after days of clashes between protesters and law enforcement officers. The mayor said the measure was necessary to ensure the safety and well-being of all residents.

The mandatory curfew covers a half-mile area surrounding the facility and took effect immediately. The order was issued on Sunday.

Protesters and police have been clashing at the site for several days. The detention center has become a flashpoint as the Trump administration increases deportation efforts.

Baraka, a Democrat, did not specify how long the curfew would remain in place or provide details about injuries or arrests during the confrontations. The curfew restricts movement in the designated area during specified hours, though the exact timeframe was not detailed in available information.

The clashes at Delaney Hall reflect broader tensions over immigration enforcement policies. Newark, New Jersey's largest city, has seen increased activity around immigration detention as federal authorities expand operations.

The mayor's decision to impose a geographic curfew rather than a citywide measure suggests officials are trying to contain the situation while minimizing disruption to the wider community. Law enforcement presence in the area has been significant as authorities work to manage the ongoing demonstrations.

The situation in Newark mirrors confrontations at other immigration facilities across the country as the administration pursues more aggressive deportation policies. Local officials in several cities have faced difficult decisions about how to balance public safety concerns with residents' rights to protest.

Baraka has not announced additional measures beyond the curfew. The restriction applies to both protesters and other residents within the half-mile radius of the detention center.

cards.headline: Iran ceasefire talks show no progress as negotiations continue
cards.teaser: Efforts to extend a ceasefire with Iran have not advanced, according to recent discussions of the diplomatic situation.
cards.body:
A report of an extended ceasefire with Iran, pending President Trump's approval, has caused global oil prices to fall. However, Trump has not yet made a decision on whether to extend the ceasefire agreement. Core issues in the negotiations remain unresolved.

Meanwhile, President Trump has offered to perform at the Freedom 250 festival, which marks America's 250th birthday. The offer comes as organizers seek to fill the event's lineup after several major musical acts withdrew from the celebration.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The Department of Justice has launched a criminal investigation originating from U.S. Attorneys offices, raising questions about the probe's origins.
cards.body:
Former federal prosecutor Ankush Khardori discussed the Justice Department's criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, calling the probe's structure uncommon. The investigation originated from U.S. Attorneys offices around the country rather than through typical channels.

Khardori, who previously worked as a federal prosecutor, explained why such investigations and prosecutions initiated at the local U.S. Attorney level are considered outside normal procedures. The case has drawn attention from legal observers tracking Justice Department activities.

cards.headline: Trump administration proposes nondisclosure agreements for federal workers
cards.teaser: The White House plan to require NDAs for government employees has drawn criticism from those who say it would silence the workforce.
cards.body:
The Office of Personnel Management proposed requiring both new and existing federal employees to sign nondisclosure agreements. The plan has generated accusations that the administration is attempting to prevent federal workers from speaking to the press.

OPM announced the proposal on Tuesday as part of efforts to manage information flow from government agencies. Critics argue the NDAs would restrict employees' ability to communicate about their work and government operations.

cards.headline: Senator Bill Cassidy holds power over health agency nominees despite Trump rift
cards.teaser: The Louisiana Republican chairs the Senate health committee as three major health agencies await permanent leadership.
cards.body:
Sen. Bill Cassidy chairs the Senate health committee, giving him authority to block nominees for three health agencies currently without permanent leaders. The Louisiana Republican is not seeking reelection and has a strained relationship with President Trump.

Cassidy's position allows him to influence which nominees advance to lead major health agencies. His decisions in the coming months will shape his legacy as he prepares to leave office, with the potential to either approve or obstruct the administration's health policy leadership.

cards.headline: Texas Senate race faces uncertainty as population grows by 2.5 million since 2020
cards.teaser: New residents and shifting Latino support for Trump have changed the political landscape in the typically Republican state.
cards.body:
Texas added more than 2.5 million residents since 2020, equivalent to New Mexico's entire population, reshaping the electorate ahead of this year's Senate race. Republican Ken Paxton remains favored to defeat Democrat James Talarico in November, but demographic changes have altered traditional political calculations.

The state gained nearly 400,000 residents in 2025 alone, more than any other state. The influx of new arrivals, combined with declining Latino support for President Trump and growth in exurban counties, has introduced new variables into what has historically been a reliably red state.

cards.headline: Iowa primary highlights state's importance for congressional control
cards.teaser: Both parties see competitive midterm races in Iowa as key to winning House and Senate majorities.
cards.body:
Iowa holds its primary election Tuesday, drawing significant attention from both Democrats and Republicans who view the state as crucial to their efforts to control Congress. While Iowa is traditionally known for its role in presidential politics, the state has become surprisingly competitive in this midterm cycle, making it a focal point for both parties' strategies.

The primary results will help shape the general election landscape as Democrats and Republicans battle for congressional majorities.
